{{Short description|none}}

The following is a list of [[United States]] cities, towns, and census-designated places in which a majority (over 50%) of the population is [[Hispanic and Latino Americans|Hispanic or Latino]], according to data from the [[United States 2000 census|2000 Census]].<ref name="GR2">{{cite web|url=https://www.census.gov|publisher=[[United States Census Bureau]]|accessdate=2008-01-31|title=U.S. Census website}}</ref><ref>United States City and Town Demographics - Wikipedia.</ref>  This list does not include cities such as [[Los Angeles, California]] or [[Houston, Texas]] in which, according to the 2000 Census, merely a plurality (as opposed to a majority) of the residents are Hispanic.  The list below is organized by [[United States state|state]] and, within each state, by population size.  The percentage of each city's population that is Hispanic is listed in parentheses next to the city's name. The largest incorporated city with the highest proportion of Hispanics is [[Huron, California|Huron]] (population 6,306), [[California]]; according to the 2000 U.S. Census, Huron is 98.27% Hispanic. The largest city with a Hispanic majority is [[San Antonio, Texas]], and the highest percentage for any major U.S. city is [[El Paso, Texas]] at 76%.<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20200210224842/http://factfinder.census.gov/servlet/SAFFFacts?_event=&geo_id=16000US4824000&_geoContext=01000US%7C04000US48%7C16000US4824000&_street=&_county=El+Paso&_cityTown=El+Paso&_state=&_zip=&_lang=en&_sse=on&ActiveGeoDiv=&_useEV=&pctxt=fph&pgsl=160&_submenuId=factsheet_1&ds_name=ACS_2007_3YR_SAFF&_ci_nbr=null&qr_name=null&reg=null:null&_keyword=&_industry=|title=El Paso city, Texas Fact Sheet}} - American FactFinder. Retrieved April 16, 2009</ref> Thirty-one states do not have any communities that are majority-Hispanic.  The following demographics are from the 2000 census.

Note: According to the [[U.S. Census]], Hispanics can be of any [[Race (U.S. census)|race]].
